project.name: Property Abundance - Ad 4 - The Honest Cash Buyer
project.prompt_schema: json-prompting Schema B, extended with video, dialogue and stage-geometry blocks
how_to_use: Generate the hero image first, from hero_image.prompt. Pick one of six.
Send each clip as ONE request. Attach the hero image every single time.
Never attach the previous clip. Referencing the previous shot is what compounds drift.
Paste world, camera_convention, object_bible, room_bible, style, hard_rules and negative_prompt into every clip request, byte-identical.
Run clip 1 alone and check it against its verify_after_render list before generating clips 2, 3 and 4.

pace.assumed_articulation_rate: 0.30 s per word, which is 200 wpm while actually talking. This is a PLAN, not a measurement. Check it against the first render and trim lines if the model reads slower.
pace.honest_note: Overall pace is 176.1 wpm, which is below ref 6's 182, the slowest of the five references. The gap is the 4.6 s of deliberate silence: the beat before 'I'll wait' and the beat before 'I don't have one'. Those two silences are the format's whole joke. The talking-head cut of this same ad measured 191.7 wpm with no silence in it. If you would rather hit the reference band, cut both pauses and the ad lands at about 35.2 s and 192.6 wpm - but it loses the button.

source_route.conform: scale=1080:1920:flags=lanczos and -r 30 at the master stage

world.origin: The phone's base, standing on the kitchen counter.
world.axes: +X is screen right. +Y is up. +Z points out of the scene toward the camera.
world.phone_facing_vector: +Z. The face looks straight down the +Z axis, at the camera.
world.counter: Runs left to right along the back wall. Counter top is Y=0 and sits 0.9 m off the floor.
world.back_wall: 0.60 m behind the phone at Z=-0.60. The wall jack the cord runs to is on this wall.
world.window: On the left wall, screen left, at X=-1.8 m. It is the cool grey key light.
world.ceiling_bulb: Above and slightly behind the camera at Z=+1.2 m, Y=+1.6 m. Warm fill.
world.camera_side: The camera always lives in +Z space, in front of the phone. Never in -Z space. This is not optional.

camera_convention.azimuth_deg: Measured from the phone's own facing direction. 0 means the camera is dead in front of the face. Positive swings the camera toward the phone's right, which reads as screen left. Hard limit for this ad: -20 to +20.
camera_convention.elevation_deg: Positive means the camera is above the phone looking down. Negative means below, looking up.
camera_convention.distance_m: Lens to the front of the phone's face.
camera_convention.height_m: Lens height above the counter top, not above the floor.
camera_convention.lens_mm: 35 mm full-frame equivalent unless the clip says otherwise.
camera_convention.why_this_block_exists: Earlier renders put the camera on the opposite side from the direction the face was pointing. Stating azimuth in degrees measured off the face, naming the camera's half of the room, and repeating the facing contract in every clip removes the model's freedom to choose a side.

object_bible: A cream-white 1990s corded kitchen wall telephone, about 24 cm tall, yellowed with age, one hairline crack across the lower right corner of the body. It has been unhooked from the wall and stands upright on the kitchen counter, its coiled beige cord still running back to the wall jack. It is a living Pixar-style 3D cartoon character. Its two round dial buttons are its eyes, glossy and expressive, set slightly too far apart. The handset rests in its cradle and the cradle slot is its mouth, which opens and closes as it speaks. The coiled cord is its one limp arm, hanging down and curling on the counter. Soft rounded cartoon shapes, matte plastic with fine dust in the seams, warm subsurface light in the plastic. All keypad buttons are completely blank. No digits, no letters, no labels, no logos, no brand marks anywhere on the object.
room_bible: A dated suburban kitchen in an empty inherited house. Oak cabinets, a laminate counter with a chipped edge, a bare fridge with four faded tape marks where photos used to be, one window above the sink. Cool grey daylight from the window plus one warm ceiling bulb. Dust in the air. Nobody in the room at any point.

style.render: 3D Pixar-style cartoon, soft rounded forms, matte plastic with subsurface warmth
style.colorRestriction: Cream white, yellowed ivory, oak brown, cool grey window light, one warm tungsten accent. No saturated colour anywhere. No blues, no greens, no reds.
style.depth_of_field: shallow, background cabinets softly out of focus
style.grade: neutral, slightly desaturated, no stylised LUT

hard_rules: One continuous shot. No cuts, no dissolves, no transitions, no split screen.
One character only. No people, no hands, no second object with a face.
No captions, subtitles, titles, watermarks, logos, UI or numbers anywhere in frame.
The keypad buttons stay completely blank. No digits, no letters.
Objects stay exactly where they are unless the phone's own cord moves them. Nothing appears or disappears.
The phone never grows arms, legs or hands. Its only moving limb is the coiled cord.
The room, the light direction, and the phone's colour, crack and dust are identical in all four clips.
Speech is generated natively inside the clip. Do not add music.
Exactly one camera move per clip, the one named in camera.move. No second move, no handheld shake.
Do not ask questions. Do not ask for a reference image beyond the one attached.

failure_guards.seen_before: The model invented a cut inside a clip.
failure_guards.guard: hard_rules 1 and 9, plus 'cut' and 'jump cut' in negative_prompt, plus exactly one named camera move.

failure_guards.seen_before: Text and UI appeared in generated footage.

hero_image.purpose: The single source of truth for the character. Every clip request attaches this file.
hero_image.pick: the most expressive eyes, and the cleanest blank keypad

clips.facing_contract: The phone's face - its two round eyes and its cradle-slot mouth - points directly at the camera lens for every frame of this clip. The camera stays in front of the face, in +Z space. The camera never moves behind the object, never crosses to the far side of the counter, and never frames the back of the object. If the camera moves, the phone turns on the spot so its face keeps pointing at the lens. The back of the phone, the wall jack and the wall behind it are never toward the lens. The eyeline stays on the lens except in the beats this clip's ACTION names, and in those beats the head does not turn more than 20 degrees.
action: The phone speaks straight into the lens.
On the word 'offer' its eyes flick 15 degrees to its own left, then come straight back to the lens.
On 'no paper' the coiled cord lifts about 10 cm off the counter and drops again. An empty-handed shrug.
A constant idle sway of about 2 degrees throughout, as if breathing.

performance.lipsync: mouth opens and closes on every syllable. Slight imprecision is acceptable.

audio.voice: close on the microphone, small room reflection
audio.sfx: a soft plastic tap as the cord drops at the end of line 2

verify_after_render: Face points at the lens in frame 1 and in the final frame.
The camera never passes the phone. The wall jack is never toward the lens.
The cord moved exactly once, on 'no paper'.

math_build.rule: No dollar figures. Ref 2 put a price on a run-down house and invited the lowball doubt it was trying to calm.

captions.why: Ref 2 failed on thin white-on-cream text. These must read with sound off.
captions.constraint: ffmpeg on this machine is built without libfreetype and without libass, measured 2026-09-23, so drawtext and subtitles do not exist. Render caption and math cards as transparent PNGs with Pillow and composite them with overlay plus enable='between(t,a,b)', the route the 2026-09-23 edit session established.

audio_master.reference: the reference reel measured -14.34 LUFS; refs 1, 2 and 6 measured -14.2

ship_gates: Lines 7 and 8 must match your real offer formula. If it is not value minus repairs minus carry and resell, rewrite them.
[NEEDS YOUR TERM: form URL] must return HTTP 200. propertyabundanceusa.com returned HTTP 403 on 2026-09-22.
Meta Housing Special Ad Category status is unchecked.
No dollar figure, no days-to-close, no percentage anywhere, spoken or on screen.
No named competitor. Lines 4 and 5 are safe because they describe what a phone call and a yard sign do not contain, which the viewer can check for themselves.
